newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Paris stocks leap on EU optimism, rest mixed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Paris stocks leap on EU optimism, rest mixed.

text.p: European bourses started in a mixed mood on Monday with Paris soaring to a trading high on hopes of a favourable outcome to the Amsterdam EU summit but London shedding nearly one percent amid jitters over next month's British budget.

In currency markets, the dollar was steady against the mark as traders bet that improving prospects for a single European currency would result in a soft euro, making "safe haven" currencues like the dollar an attractive investment.

French stocks, hit badly by the Socialists' win in this month's election, shot up by 0.5 percent to an intra-day high of 2,825.18 points on the blue-chip CAC-40 index, cheered by a record-breaking run on Wall Street last week as well as optimism over Amsterdam.
"The dollar's steady, New York rose to a new record on Friday and for the time being investors expect there will be a deal and the market's waiting now for confirmation of an accord," a broker said.

European leaders are expected to try to accommodate France's Socialist-led government by offering vague language stressing the importance of creating jobs in European monetary union without making the kind of changes to a stability pact on fiscal discipline that would upset Germany.
But the Paris surge quickly ran out of steam and stocks lost the early gains, barely staying in profit by mid-morning.

London made the weakest showing. An impressive stock market debut for insurer Norwich Union and the rally in New York failed to outweigh nerves ahead of the new British government's first budget and the EU summit.
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares, which set three closing records last week, fell 41.6 to 4,741.5 points in early trade before regaining some of the losses.
"People are starting to get nervous," one dealer said. "Trade will be very thin."

Last week's bullish mood was dampened on talk that dividend tax benefits might be axed in the budget on July 2 in a move that would target the corporate sector rather than cooling consumer spending. Concern about the Amsterdam summit was also hurting sentiment, dealers said
One bright spot in the market was Norwich Union's market debut. Shares in the former mutually-owned insurance group opened at 356p, compared with a public offer price of 290p.
In Frankfurt, stocks made healthy gains, lifted by a near one percent jump on Wall Street on Friday and the firmer tone of the dollar, seen as helping the German exporting sector.
The DAX-30 index put on over 0.5 percent in early trade to 3,770.90 points at one point but volume was weak.

"Basically there isn't a whole lot around to talk about this morning. We're higher on the back of Wall Street and we could reach 3,800 points during bourse trade. Turnover is very thin," a Frankfurt broker said.
In currencies, the dollar slipped against the yen, as worries over U.S.-Japan trade frictions refused to go away, but held last week's gains on the mark.
The dollar was at 1.7345 marks, nearly two pfennigs above the levels seen for much of last week, but slipped to 113.99 yen, nearly a yen below the range in late European trading on Friday.

Analysts said improving prospects for an EU deal would bolster the dollar against the mark as speculation took hold abut a weak single currency but gains are not likely to be great as a deal is largely priced in.

In Europe, the focus was firmly on the two-day Amsterdam summit. Comments from European officials raised hopes of an accord on the so-called stability pact -- designed to stop countries running big deficits after EMU begins.
"All eyes are on Amsterdam -- that's going to overshadow any data from the U.S. for the next couple of days," said Elizabeth Cheale, trader at Dresdner Bank in London.

"It looks as if they're going to reach agreement today or tomorrow, which makes a softer euro more likely. That means there is a lack of confidence in the mark and is making the dollar, French franc and Swiss franc all the more attractive," he said.
The dollar was not expected to make much headway against the yen as last week's fears lingered about U.S.-Japanese trade friction ahead of a Group of Seven summit in Denver on June 20-22.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7345 marks and 113.99 yen, compared with 1.7373 and 114.73 in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 34.7 points at 4748.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 5.16 points at 2813.68.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 21.75 points at 3766.19.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $340.95 an ounce, compared with Friday's close of $341.55.
